title: Chandra Dynasty
capsule: The Chandra dynasty was a Buddhist royal house that ruled Samatata (southeastern Bengal) and adjacent coastal territories from roughly the late ninth to mid-eleventh century. Founded around 900 CE, the dynasty made its capital at Vikrampur and patronised Tantric Buddhism, becoming a conduit for Mahayana transmission into Southeast Asia and Arakan. At its apogee under rulers such as Srichandra and Kalyanachandra, the kingdom maintained diplomatic ties with the Pala Empire to its west. The dynasty collapsed around 1050–1056 under pressure from the Varman dynasty and Chola naval incursions, disappearing from the inscriptional record.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Chandra dynasty's territorial extent rests on a limited corpus of copper-plate grants and coins; boundaries with contemporary Pala and Varman territories are reconstructed and subject to revision.
